entries.name: Reformed Theological Seminary
entries.location: Jackson, MS; Orlando, FL; Charlotte, NC; Atlanta, GA; Washington, D.C.; Global (online)
entries.affiliation: Nondenominational; serves primarily the PCA, also the EPC, ARP, Reformed Baptist and independent churches
entries.doctrinal_basis: Each trustee, senior administrator and voting faculty member subscribes to a Statement of Belief and Covenant affirming biblical inerrancy and the Westminster Standards (RTS, “Reaching Our Standards”).
points_to_weigh: Nondenominational: its campuses draw students from several denominations, not only the PCA or OPC.
2010: professor Bruce Waltke resigned after remarks on evolution made to the BioLogos Foundation (Wikipedia).
entries.description: Reformed seminary founded by conservatives from the Presbyterian Church in the United States, with residential campuses and a Global online campus.

entries.name: Westminster Theological Seminary
entries.doctrinal_basis: All trustees and faculty must affirm the Westminster Confession of Faith and the Larger and Shorter Catechisms (Wikipedia).
points_to_weigh: Founded in 1929 by Princeton Seminary faculty, including J. Gresham Machen, who opposed that seminary's modernist reorganization.
Documented faculty disputes over theological direction: Norman Shepherd (1981, justification), Peter Enns (2008, Old Testament interpretation), and Douglas Green (2014).
entries.description: Reformed seminary founded in response to the 1929 reorganization of Princeton Seminary; offers online master's and doctoral programs taught by the same faculty.

entries.name: Westminster Seminary California
entries.affiliation: Multi-denominational Reformed and Presbyterian; close ties to the PCA, OPC and URCNA
entries.doctrinal_basis: All faculty and trustees sign the Westminster Standards and the Three Forms of Unity before installation (WSC, Doctrinal Standards).
points_to_weigh: Known for teaching the Reformed “two kingdoms” doctrine, sometimes called “Escondido theology” (Wikipedia).
entries.description: Confessional Reformed seminary that emphasizes in-person education, with audit opportunities.

entries.name: Covenant Theological Seminary
entries.doctrinal_basis: Faculty must subscribe to the Westminster Standards (Wikipedia).
points_to_weigh: 2018: the Revoice conference met at Memorial Presbyterian Church in St. Louis. The seminary's president said Covenant was not an official sponsor, but a seminary vice president spoke there. In March 2019 the president announced that no faculty would take part in the 2019 conference (Christian Post; byFaith).

entries.name: Reformed Presbyterian Theological Seminary
entries.founded: Classes began in 1810, soon after the RPCNA was organized in Philadelphia in 1798
entries.affiliation: Reformed Presbyterian Church of North America (RPCNA)
entries.doctrinal_basis: A ministry of the RPCNA, which holds the Westminster Standards and the RPCNA Testimony. The seminary describes its education as within ‘the framework of the historic Reformed faith’.
points_to_weigh: Denominational seminary: it is closely tied to the RPCNA, whose worship is exclusive psalmody without instruments; confirm what this means for students and faculty with the seminary.
Its emphasis is pastoral: all professors have significant field experience in the church and it uses the motto ‘Study under pastors’.
Its graduates serve churches of many denominations, though most are pastors and preachers, according to the seminary.
Delivery formats and tuition were not on the page reviewed.
degrees: Graduate Theological Studies Diploma (graduate courses for credit without a full degree)
entries.accreditation: Fully accredited by the Association of Theological Schools (ATS)
entries.description: The RPCNA's seminary, which says its 1810 start makes it the fourth oldest seminary in the nation. Its mission is to educate students who love the Lord Jesus Christ and His Word and equip pastors, within the framework of the historic Reformed faith.

entries.name: Mid-America Reformed Seminary
entries.affiliation: United Reformed Churches in North America; also serves the OPC, PCA, CRC and RCUS
entries.doctrinal_basis: Adheres to the ecumenical creeds and the Reformed confessions (Belgic Confession, Heidelberg Catechism, Canons of Dort, Westminster Confession); faculty and trustees are committed to the inerrancy of Scripture (Wikipedia).
points_to_weigh: Small institution (about 30 students and 6 faculty as reported); operates independently rather than under denominational governance.
entries.description: Continental Reformed seminary serving the URCNA and other confessional churches.

entries.location: Due West, Columbia and Greenville, SC

entries.name: The Master's Seminary
entries.affiliation: Grace Community Church and The Master's University (John MacArthur)
entries.doctrinal_basis: Doctrinal statement affirms biblical inerrancy, Reformed soteriology and dispensational premillennialism (Wikipedia); faculty affirm it in writing.
points_to_weigh: Dispensational premillennial rather than covenantal, so it differs from the Westminster Standards on eschatology and church government.
2018–2020: WSCUC placed The Master's University and Seminary on probation over governance concerns; the sanction was lifted in November 2020 (Wikipedia).

entries.name: Princeton Theological Seminary
entries.doctrinal_basis: A PC(USA) seminary; it operates under the PC(USA)'s Book of Confessions rather than the Westminster Standards alone.
points_to_weigh: Affiliated with the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.), not the PCA or OPC. The PC(USA) has permitted ordination of openly gay and lesbian officers since 2011 and defined marriage as between two persons since 2015 (Wikipedia: PC(USA)).
Reorganized along modernist lines in 1929, which led J. Gresham Machen and colleagues to found Westminster Theological Seminary (Wikipedia).
entries.description: PC(USA) seminary. Listed so readers can recognize it as distinct from PCA- and OPC-aligned seminaries.
